name: Social Liberalism
summary: Social liberalism keeps the liberal commitment to individual freedom, equal rights and representative government, but holds that real freedom needs favorable social and economic conditions. It therefore backs a mixed, regulated market economy, a welfare state, progressive taxation and action against poverty, while rejecting revolutionary socialism and central planning.
scope: The new-liberal and social-liberal mainstream: T. H. Green, L. T. Hobhouse and J. A. Hobson, the Edwardian Liberal reforms, Keynes and Beveridge, German social liberalism (Naumann), and the egalitarian liberalism of John Rawls, Dworkin and Sen. It excludes classical or neoliberal free-market liberalism and social democracy proper. Many cultural and foreign-policy questions are not addressed in the core texts, so those answers are low-confidence inferences from modern social-liberal parties and general principles.

keyFigures.name: L. T. Hobhouse
keyFigures.role: Author of Liberalism (1911), a defining statement of the new liberalism.

keyFigures.name: T. H. Green
keyFigures.role: Philosopher of positive liberty whose ideas shaped the new liberals.

keyFigures.name: John Rawls
keyFigures.role: Author of A Theory of Justice (1971), combining equal liberties with fairer distribution.

sources.usedFor: Rawlsian liberties, equality of opportunity, difference principle, property-owning democracy, Law of Peoples.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The welfare state, including health insurance and care, is a defining social liberal aim, from the 1911 Liberal reforms to Beveridge; Rawls's state guarantees health care.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Hobhouse treats a living wage as a right as valid as property rights; a substantial rise is a typical application but the size is not specified.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Hobhouse argues real bargaining needs rough equality, so markets need state correction; social liberals still value markets, hence mild disagreement.

public-ownership.rationale: Social liberals favor a mixed economy and regulated capitalism rather than broad nationalization, though some utilities may be public.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Progressive taxation was central to the 1909 People's Budget and to solidarist thought.

unions-good.rationale: Hobhouse sees legal emancipation of unions as liberating because collective bargaining equalizes bargaining power.

property-fundamental.rationale: Hobhouse questions the classical assumption that property rights are beyond question and allows taxing and regulating them.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulated capitalism and correcting market failures are core to the social market economy.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare provision is a defining commitment; social liberals reject cuts of this kind.

worker-ownership.rationale: Rawls allows worker-managed firms as one option, but most social liberals prefer mixed ownership with private firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Priority of basic liberties implies suspicion of mass surveillance, though security trade-offs are accepted by some.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Hobhouse limits liberty only where others are injured; adults' drug use follows by inference, and adherents vary.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Hobhouse protects speech and worship except for injury or disorder; adherents split on hate-speech law, with civil liberties leaning against.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberalism opposes concentrated unaccountable power; Hobhouse ties it to law and responsible government.

state-harmful.rationale: Hobhouse rejects abolishing the state's machinery and sees the state as securing conditions for freedom.

limit-guns.rationale: Contemporary social liberal parties generally back stricter gun controls; the classic texts do not address it.

empower-police-military.rationale: Hobhouse warns of militarism as a threat to free institutions; infers skepticism of expanded powers.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from limiting liberty only for harm to others; adherents are divided over exploitation concerns.

decide-locally.rationale: Social liberals tend to want national welfare standards, though they value dispersed power.

rehabilitation.rationale: Reform-minded liberalism favors rehabilitation; inferred, not specifically sourced.

traditional-family.rationale: Social liberals favor personal autonomy in family forms; inferred from modern parties' positions.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Modern social liberalism in the American sense includes support for same-sex marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reproductive rights are listed among social liberal positions in American usage.

more-religion-public.rationale: Rawlsian public reason asks public justification in shared terms, which limits a larger religious role in public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Fair equality of opportunity requires more than anti-discrimination; social liberals support active remedies, though not all forms.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed in core texts; adherents divided between cultural and mixed views.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Liberals value open, pluralist society over preserving national tradition; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Reformist and incremental but not deferential to established institutions; adherents split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Internationalist liberal outlook leans against restriction; adherents vary.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Social liberalism is generally internationalist, and Rawls accommodates bodies like the UN.

free-trade.rationale: Social liberals value open trade but stress compensating losers; contested among adherents.

nation-first.rationale: Internationalism and Hobhouse's opposition to force make nation-first stances alien to it.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Rawls permits intervention for grave human rights violations.

open-borders.rationale: Rawls assumes closed societies; most social liberals favor regulated but generous migration rather than open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Environmentalism exists in the tradition (Freiburg Thesis) but growth is not opposed as such.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The Freiburg Thesis put environmental protection ahead of profit, and parties champion climate action.

revolution-justified.rationale: Hobhouse rejects the class-war framing and the use of force; reform through law is preferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Democratization is central to the case for an active state; some technocratic leaning exists, so only mild.

central-planning.rationale: Hobhouse explicitly rejects Marxist central control of the economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Rawls accepts liberal socialism as one regime, but social liberals mostly accept private ownership too.

land-value-tax.rationale: Georgist ideas influenced New Liberals but not a core commitment today.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Rawls's justice requires regulating inheritance; Hobhouse allows taxing property; amount is unclear.

basic-income.rationale: Rawls favors a social minimum; form (unconditional) is debated among adherents.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Keynesian demand management is accepted but not directing strategic industries; inferred.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rawls's property-owning democracy aims at wide dispersal of capital.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Hobhouse remunerates in proportion to service and keeps the market economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Keynesian economics relies on state macro management.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Hobhouse favors union bargaining but not state-run wage and price setting.

one-party-rule.rationale: Equal basic liberties and fair political liberties are incompatible with one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Many social liberal parties exist in constitutional monarchies; the statement is split.

democracy-best.rationale: Representative democratic constitutions are central, as in Weimar German democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Favors representative government in the sources, not direct lawmaking.

right-to-secede.rationale: Rawls's liberal peoples are constitutional democracies; no stated secession right.

natural-rulers.rationale: Hobhouse opposes hereditary and class barriers to occupations and equal legal rights.

political-violence-never.rationale: Hobhouse opposes force as the basis of tyranny, but liberalism accepts resistance to tyranny in some cases.

war-builds-character.rationale: Hobhouse calls opposing force essential to liberalism and sees militarism as a threat.

separate-church-state.rationale: Religious freedom and public reason support separation, with accommodation in some countries.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Public reason requires justification by shared public values.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Law applied equally by the state is basic to Hobhouse's liberty.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Equal rights regardless of class or origin; inferred ethnic exclusivity is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hobhouse rejects the class-war framing of Marxism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Difference principle permits inequalities benefiting the worst off; equality of opportunity is emphasized over equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed in sources; adherents split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Internationalism is broader than civilizational blocs; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Hobhouse warns against confusing liberty with competition and stresses community; inferred.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individual rights and liberties come first; Rawls gives basic liberties priority.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental duty to future generations; intrinsic value is not specified.

limit-population.rationale: Liberal autonomy opposes coercive limits; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Social liberalism seeks to reform, not reject, industrial economy.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The core texts say nothing on technological pace, and adherents are split between enthusiasm and caution.

human-enhancement.rationale: Autonomy supports freedom but adherents have bioethical worries.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Pragmatic reform is valued, but principles are central; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Hobhouse rejects force and values law; consistent with this.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rejected by any reformist industrial-era ideology.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hobhouse's liberal socialism keeps wage labor and occupations.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Hobhouse ties remuneration to social service, not need alone.

production-for-use.rationale: Market and enterprise are retained with regulation.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Hobhouse rejects Marxist exploitation framing but sees unequal bargaining producing abuse.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Hobhouse rejects Marxist socialism and its control of the economy.

collective-farming.rationale: Not compatible with private property and market structure.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Hobhouse opposes militarism but rejects Marxist determinism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Taxation funds welfare and public goods and is central to the program.

harm-principle.rationale: Hobhouse limits liberty where others are injured, though social liberals accept some further grounds like education.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rights are individual but community and welfare rights are also stressed.

conscription.rationale: Hobhouse's opposition to militarism and Rawls's basic liberties argue against conscription.

state-as-business.rationale: The state's role is to enable citizens, not serve customers.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Equal opportunity and anti-hereditary-privilege stance rejects racial hierarchies.

total-state.rationale: Hobhouse limits the state to securing conditions of liberty and values personal liberty.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Equal rule of law is basic.

bound-labor.rationale: Hobhouse opposes serfdom-like barriers; liberty is to be controlled by no other man.

universal-morality.rationale: Rawls seeks an overlapping consensus, not a metaphysical universal truth; Hobhouse had an ethical rational view.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The core texts do not address this, and social liberals are divided on it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The core texts do not address this, and social liberals are divided on it.

revive-national-language.rationale: The core texts do not address this, and adherents have no common position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rawls favors worker-managed firms in liberal socialism; mild support for participation.

school-vouchers.rationale: Rawls favors state-funded high-quality education; vouchers are contested.

economic-freedom.rationale: Hobhouse stresses that liberty needs economic conditions provided by the state rather than economic freedom alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: German and other liberal tradition supports self-government; limited here.

force-without-un.rationale: Internationalist and institutional preference; Rawls allows intervention only for grave abuses.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Liberals value reason but accept religious freedom and faith in public life; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare is rights-based and universal in outlook; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Hobhouse wants state to enable self-support rather than provide directly; split on conditions.

class-collaboration.rationale: Naumann aimed to reduce class conflict without revolution; Hobhouse rejects class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Reformist liberals do not favor destroying inherited institutions.

workers-nation.rationale: Not a social liberal stance; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Green and Hobhouse hold that liberty needs favorable social and economic conditions, the basis for an active state.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social liberalism upholds equal rights under law, and modern social-liberal parties back gender equality; inferred from Rawls equal basic liberties.

ban-interest.rationale: Social liberals support a regulated mixed market economy that includes credit and finance; Hobhouse and Keynes saw interest as a market tool to manage, not ban.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Rawls equal basic liberties and equal citizenship exclude racial classification and legal separation, and social-liberal parties oppose it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Hobhouse sees the state as the means to secure common welfare and equal liberty, not a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not addressed in the core texts; inferred from modern social-liberal parties, which back climate action and a managed transition.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Rawlsian pluralism and social-liberal parties favour integration while respecting cultural diversity; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: social liberals explain immigration by economic and social forces and reject conspiracy claims.

proportional-representation.rationale: Modern social-liberal parties generally favour proportional representation as fairer; the core texts do not address it, so inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Social liberals favour liberal-democratic cooperation, not a national mission to export government; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Rawls's basic structure includes the family and institutions that must be fair; social liberals back correcting disadvantages, so structural disadvantage for women is accepted. Inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Social liberals favour accountable, active government and do not hold that elites are mostly corrupt; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Rawls's equal basic liberties exclude coercion over reproduction; some Edwardian new liberals backed eugenics, so this is a modern-focused inference.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Rule of law and equal rights under justice as fairness imply accountability for state abuses; modern social-liberal parties back international courts.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Social liberals explicitly reject the minimal state: the 1911 case for liberty rests on state action to secure social conditions.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed in the core texts; inferred from the liberal commitment to individual choice and equal rights.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rawls and the new liberals treat persons as free and equal moral persons with equal basic rights.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the rejection of revolutionary socialism and Rawls's Law of Peoples, which has no spreading revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not addressed in the core texts; social liberals are divided on how to classify settler states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from equal citizenship in Rawls, though social liberals also respect pluralism of communities.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from the liberal commitment to liberty of conscience, which Rawls lists among the basic liberties.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred from liberty of conscience and the harm principle, which give little ground for a ban founded on religious reverence.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from Rawlsian public reason and the separation of church and state favoured by social liberal parties.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of central planning and revolutionary socialism, and from favouring accountable government.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rawls and the liberal tradition ground legitimate authority in the agreement of free and equal citizens.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Inferred from the Enlightenment commitment to reasoned public argument and evidence; the tradition does not treat knowledge as a mere product of power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Inferred: liberal internationalism favors open trade and treats the trade balance as no national goal.

population-transfer.rationale: Equal individual rights and minority protection are core liberal commitments, which rule out expelling a minority.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Hobhouse opposes force in politics, but social liberals accept coercive taxation and regulation for social ends, so the ban is not absolute.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Inferred: Hobhouse and the new liberals rejected laissez-faire struggle in favor of cooperation and social harmony.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Inferred: modern social-liberal parties generally accept defending a liberal constitutional order against parties that would abolish it.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Green and Hobhouse hold that economic dependence and unequal bargaining power undermine liberty even without direct coercion.

separated-powers.rationale: Constitutional government with checks on power is basic to liberalism, including Rawls's constitutional democracy.

vanguard-party.rationale: Social liberals reject revolutionary socialism; Hobhouse opposes Marxism and class revolution in favor of reform through representative politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Rawls's difference principle ranks the position of the least advantaged first among inequalities, and the welfare state targets poverty.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Social liberals favour broad ownership but also public provision; the core texts do not address council housing, so adherents split.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Hobhouse defends unions and the right to combine; mainstream social liberals accept some ballot rules but oppose curbing strikes, inferred from this.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Social liberals trace poverty to social and economic conditions, not numbers; inferred from Hobhouse and Green on social causes.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Social-liberal parties embrace pluralism and integration; inferred from general principles of equal rights.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Social liberals favour representative elected government; lotteries are not part of the tradition, so this is inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Rawls and the liberal tradition hold that basic liberties and legal protections are not to be suspended lightly, even under pressure.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Mixed-economy liberals accept some intervention but generally prefer market prices, inferred from Keynesian and Beveridge-era practice.

party-controls-media.rationale: Liberal commitment to free expression and independent press is central; Hobhouse opposes coercion in opinion.

party-commands-army.rationale: Representative liberal government keeps the army under the state and constitution, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Social liberals favour inclusion but accept residence requirements; adherents split on length, so the answer is inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Social liberals do not take a stated position on official pay; adherents split between ordinary pay and pay that attracts talent, inferred from general principles.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Liberal parties typically allow conscience votes and prize individual judgment; inferred from the liberal commitment to individual freedom.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Social-liberal parties are internationalist and widely back European integration and shared institutions, per the overview of the tradition.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Liberal constitutionalism favors accountable, parliamentary government over executive command; inferred, as core texts do not address it.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Liberalism separates church and state and leaves church governance to believers; inferred, so no clear stance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Liberalism's commitment to equal liberties and secular representative government rejects rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Hobhouse's liberalism opposed force and militarism and favored internationalism, but defeating one's own government in wartime was not a social-liberal position; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Rawls's equal basic liberties include free expression, which censorship for moral character would violate.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Social liberalism has no stated view on re-election limits; adherents are split between voter choice and term-limit safeguards, inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Accountable representative government is core, and recall is a common democratic tool; inferred, as core texts do not address it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Social-liberal parties generally back alliances such as NATO and multilateral order; inferred from modern party practice, as the core texts are silent.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Social liberals accept private property and regulate rather than abolish renting; inferred from the reformist, non-socialist stance.

people-in-arms.rationale: Social liberals favor professional, state-controlled forces and gun regulation; inferred from modern party positions.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The tradition is urban and progress-minded and treats place of living as a matter of choice; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Social liberalism does not address border reunification; it supports self-determination, but answers would depend on the case.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Social liberals prize education and expertise as tools of reform; Green and Hobhouse backed expanded education, and the claim is inferred to be rejected.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Modern social liberals lean to cultural pluralism and equal respect (Rawls on reasonable pluralism), but classic new liberals held developmental views; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Social-liberal parties mostly oppose capital punishment on human-rights grounds; inferred from party practice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Social-liberal parties support sex education and gender equality in public schools; inferred from modern party practice and the equal-rights tradition.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Social liberals back secular, science-based public education; inferred from the tradition's rationalism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social liberals defend civil liberties and generally resist censorship of adult material, while supporting protections for minors; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Modern social-liberal parties favor birthright or residence-based paths to citizenship; inferred from party practice.

minority-language-support.rationale: Social liberalism's pluralism and equal-opportunity aims support minority language rights; inferred from modern party positions.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Social liberals value freedom of conscience but also equal application of law, and Rawls allows limits; adherents are split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The liberal tradition from Mill values individuality and experiments in living, and Green and Hobhouse linked liberty to self-development.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Rawls's Law of Peoples holds a duty to assist burdened societies, which supports debt relief; inferred, since the core texts do not address it.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Social liberals favour reform within a mixed market economy and not transforming the ownership system; inferred from their rejection of revolutionary socialism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Social liberals back representative government and constitutional democracy but have no settled view on rewriting a constitution by assembly; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Rawls gives the basic liberties priority over economic advantage and the liberal tradition rejects trading them for growth.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Rawls's Law of Peoples sets a duty of assistance to burdened societies, and social-liberal parties support development aid, though Rawls limits the duty.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Social-liberal parties are split between alliance-based defence and disarmament and the core texts do not address it; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Social liberals accept both parliamentary and presidential models and the core texts are silent; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Keynesian social liberals accept central bank independence in practice but want monetary policy to serve employment as well as prices; adherents are split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Internationalist social-liberal parties generally favour negotiated settlements including territorial compromise; inferred from their internationalism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Hobhouse and the new liberals hold that property is a social function whose use the community may regulate for the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Social liberals reject Soviet communism but the state-capitalist label is a Marxist-dissident debate they rarely engage in; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the acceptance of regulation to protect the public and the environment.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the internationalism of social-liberal parties, which generally back alliances such as NATO.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Hobhouse opposed imperial force, and Rawls and social-liberal internationalism rest on self-determination.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred: secular state and church-state separation, but religious liberty is protected and suppression of churches is not liberal.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from constitutional government, where the head of state is a neutral symbol; presidential parties vary.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from self-determination and Rawls on peoples, though many parties defend territorial integrity.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the support of social-liberal parties for devolution and federalism.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Liberalism rests on equal rights and representative government, so a divine-descent ruler is rejected.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation is a core social-liberal position, justified by equal opportunity and the difference principle.

character-from-environment.rationale: Green and Hobhouse held that conditions shape persons, which is why they argued for social reform; Rawls treats natural endowments as morally arbitrary.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rule of law and constitutional government are basic liberal commitments shared with the social strand.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred: not addressed by the tradition and mixed among adherents, with priority generally given to social needs.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred: social liberals favour representative democracy with checks, not a blend of few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Hobhouse's opposition to force and personal rule, and liberal democratic norms, reject glorifying a leader.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred: parties are split, with some backing shared parenting and others a best-interests test.

missingStatements.text: Freedom requires that people have the material means to act on it, not only the absence of interference.
missingStatements.rationale: Hobhouse and Green hold that liberty depends on social and economic conditions, which justifies an active state.

notes: American usage of liberal often means progressive on social issues, and strands differ: Rawlsians lean to property-owning democracy, others to a Keynesian welfare state.
